hypotheses.title: Missing upgrade authorization allows arbitrary contract upgrades
hypotheses.description: The contract inherits `UUPSUpgradeable` but does not override the internal `_authorizeUpgrade` function, which is required to restrict upgrades to privileged accounts. Consequently, any external address can invoke `upgradeTo` or `upgradeToAndCall` on the proxy and replace the implementation with a malicious contract, gaining full control over the staking logic and assets.
hypotheses.attackPath: 1. Attacker calls `upgradeTo(address maliciousImpl)` on the proxy contract. 2. Because `_authorizeUpgrade` is empty, the call succeeds without any permission check. 3. The malicious implementation includes functions to drain `rewardsReserve`, transfer staked tokens, or alter ownership, allowing the attacker to exfiltrate all funds.
hypotheses.impact: Total loss of user‑deposited tokens and rewards; attacker gains complete control over the protocol.
hypotheses.recommendation: Override `_authorizeUpgrade` with an access‑controlled modifier, e.g., `function _authorizeUpgrade(address) internal override onlyOwner {}` (or a multisig/governance check).
